verdicts.reason: Quote states sampling every read clock, latency 1, resetless array. Assertion on data is checkable.
Tie-off is internal structure of wrapper, not checkable from interface signals every cycle.
Write behavior stated in quote; checkable at the macro interface.
Read behavior stated explicitly with latency and hold.
Stated in quote; needs a directed scenario for same-address read/write.
Structural statement, quote supports it; nothing to check dynamically.
Pure description of the model implementation; nothing to verify or exercise beyond the behavior already covered by rules 32/33.
Reject and overflow raised on write while full are stated.
Reject and underflow on read while empty are stated.
Allowed concurrent operation with independent response; a scenario to exercise, not an assertion. MAY with scenario is fine; keep MAY but actor is the FIFO not any.
Stated in quote; the handshake sequence requires scenario.
Not accepted and no error pulse stated; checkable by assertion and scenario.
Sampling edge convention, not an assertable behavior; a testbench convention.
Quote states no hold required; scenario of changing data after the edge.
Description of absence of an output; nothing to verify or exercise.
Integrator guidance outside the IP; nothing to verify.

questions.question: Does a rejected write while full or read while empty also leave the pointers and stored data completely unchanged, and are overflow/underflow single-cycle pulses or sticky flags? The quote does not give pulse width or clock domain.
During software reset, are writes/reads blocked from the start of i_rst_n_sw assertion or only after the handshake completes? Section 10.7 is referenced but not quoted.
